title: A queue from two stacks
hook: Taking from the wrong end means flipping everything. Or does it?

knows: a stack gives back the last thing added; a queue gives back the first (back-button-stack)
an occasional big copy can average out over many operations (list-doubling-copies)
doesNotKnow: that a queue can be built from two stacks cheaply
that each item is poured at most once

misconception: A queue made of two stacks must flip everything over on every removal.
objective: The learner can explain that with two stacks, an item is poured from the in-stack to the out-stack at most once in its life, so one slow removal pays for the fast ones and the average cost stays constant.

claims.text: For the tape add 1, add 2, remove, add 3, add 4, remove, remove, remove (pop the out-stack; pour the whole in-stack over only when the out-stack is empty) there are exactly 2 pours: the first moves 2 then 1, the second moves 4 then 3; every item is moved once (each 'moved' badge stops at 1), 4 moves in total, and the items leave in the order 1 2 3 4.
claims.source: simulate() in Demo.tsx v3 with OPS = add, add, rem, add, add, rem, rem, rem; traced by hand 2026-10-14 by the builder (not a verification). | Builder's node script (2026-10-14), written from the rule in the question: pours 1, moved {1:1, 2:1, 3:1, 4:1}, left order 1,2,3,4. The first removal pours 4, 3, 2, 1 (1 ends on top); removals 2 to 4 find the out-stack non-empty. Demo.tsx runs the same rule. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Own node sim of the rule: 1 pour, moved {1:1,2:1,3:1,4:1}, left 1 2 3 4; matches simulate() and the reveal. | REOPENED 2026-10-14 (v3, wave D r5 revision by demo-builder): learner-visible sentence changed; needs a fresh check. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own node trace of the v3 tape: pours at tile 3 (moves 2 then 1) and tile 7 (moves 4 then 3); moved {1:1,2:1,3:1,4:1}; 4 moves; left 1 2 3 4.

claims.text: An item crosses from the in-stack to the out-stack at most once in its life, so a slow removal pays for the fast ones around it and the average cost per operation stays constant (amortized O(1)).
claims.source: CLRS 3rd ed., exercise 10.1-6 (implement a queue using two stacks) and chapter 17, accounting method: charge each item 1 extra unit when added to pay for its single later move. Derivation: an item is only ever moved from in to out, and nothing moves from out back to in. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Derivation: items move only in->out, so moves <= adds (own random sim of 100,000 ops confirms). CLRS 3e exercise 10.1-6 and ch. 17 accounting method (4e: ch. 16). | REOPENED 2026-10-14 (v3, wave D r5 revision by demo-builder): learner-visible sentence changed; needs a fresh check. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Derivation: items move only in->out, so moves <= adds (own random 100,000-op sim). CLRS 3e ex. 10.1-6 and ch. 17 from my knowledge, not opened; the sentence rests on the derivation.

claims.text: A removal that finds the out-stack not empty needs no pour.
claims.source: It follows from the rule in the question: the pour happens only when the out-stack is empty. Stage text 'out not empty: no pour' on removals 2 to 4. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Direct from the rule; stage note 'out not empty: no pour' on removals 2-4.

claims.text: This is the same accounting as list doubling.
claims.source: In list doubling (lesson list-doubling-copies) an occasional big copy is paid for by cheap adds in between; here an occasional pour is paid for by cheap removals. Both are the accounting method (CLRS ch. 17). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Both are the accounting method (CLRS 3e 17.2, dynamic tables 17.4); lesson list-doubling-copies exists in src/demos/cs.

claims.text: The second pour never touched 1 or 2: they had already crossed to out and left.
claims.source: Trace of simulate() in Demo.tsx: after the first removal out holds [2]; the second removal pops 2 without a pour; the third removal finds out empty and pours in = [3, 4]. Reveal paragraph 2. | Added 2026-10-14 (v3) by demo-builder. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own trace: at the second pour (the 3rd removal, tile 7) both 1 and 2 have already LEFT; out is empty, which is why it pours. So '(1 has left, 2 is in out)' is false at that moment, and the reveal's 'they were already in out' reads as if they sat in out during the pour. Fix (builder): 'The second pour never touched 1 or 2: they had already crossed to out and left.' | Builder fix (demo-builder, 2026-10-14): W-213: reveal and claim now use the fact-checker's wording; at the second pour (3rd removal, tile 7) both 1 and 2 have already been removed and out is empty. | FC pass 23 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own node trace of the tape. Tile 3 pours 2 then 1, and 1 leaves. Tile 6 pops 2, no pour. Tile 7 pours 4 then 3, and at that moment 1 and 2 have both already left, so out is empty and holds only 3 and 4 after the pour. 'Crossed to out and left' is true for both: each crossed in the first pour. The reveal (line 246) uses the pass 22 wording word for word.

recall.question: A queue is built from two stacks. You add 1000 items, then remove them all. Roughly how many times is each item moved between stacks?
options: Once for every removal before it
recall.why: The first removal pours all 1000 items into the out-stack, once each. After that every removal just pops the out-stack, so no item moves again.
